findings.obligation: D16 (docs/feature/iis-slack-replace-remove/architecture.md, governed slices S1, S2, S3): the notice a stored Slack change earned waits as a one-shot value under one session key and is taken out as the page reads it, so an address alone - typed again, bookmarked or shared - carries neither a submitted value nor a notice and claims no change that was not made. A user-visible claim a design decision makes needs a case the oracle can observe.
findings.observation: Severity low, non-blocking, owner oracle; carried forward from runs/review.oracle.S1.json and review.oracle.S3.json and confirmed open at 299f6e0 by this reviewer. Only the positive half of D16 is observed: every scenario that reads I-10, I-16 or I-17 follows the redirect and finds the notice (GREEN in R15, R16). Nothing observes the negative half. No scenario in crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/instance-integration-setup.feature opens the landed page a second time or reaches it by address alone to read that the notice is gone, then_on_instance_page (support/instance_integration_setup.rs:1429) compares only answer.path.split('?').next() with the instance path, which a '?saved=...' address satisfies too, and no recorded unit row covers SavedNotice::taken_from. A handler that kept the notice in the address, or left it in the session for every later read, would pass the whole recorded oracle. This reviewer verified the shipped mechanism by reading it (handlers/instance.rs:422-439 and :846: insert on the wire name, remove on the read, no query source left under crates), so this is an unobserved promise, not a defect in the product, and the original Request states no obligation about addresses or notices on reload - hence non-blocking.
findings.remediation: The acceptance designer adds one case that reads the page a second time after a change - a plain GET of /admin/instance/integrations following the landing read, expecting the page with no notice - and binds D16 to it, or an equivalent row over SavedNotice::taken_from; alternatively the architect narrows D16 to the redirect it actually promises. No production change is implied either way.

findings.observation: Severity low, non-blocking, owner oracle; carried forward from runs/review.oracle.S3.json finding 1 and confirmed open at 299f6e0. The only test F203 cites is the public scenario 'Remove says how many workspaces stop posting, and reading it removes nothing', whose closing step then_saved_app_unchanged reads the page, both secrets, the activity list, Add to Slack and a verifying event - never the configuration version. The version clause does have a witness: handlers/instance.rs:1934 the_table_of_what_the_confirm_and_remove_pages_reach_when_they_are_only_read asserts ReadOnlyDoor::SlackRemove.reads() == [PageRead::ConnectedWorkspaces] and ReadOnlyDoor::read (:525) makes exactly the calls in that list, so a GET of the remove door can write nothing at all; it ran GREEN in R13. The gap is the citation, not the coverage.
findings.remediation: The acceptance designer cites the handler read-table row beside the public scenario for L6/F203, or extends the scenario's closing step to read the configuration version. No production change.

Corrected delta judged finding by finding against the rejected round. Finding 1 (blocker, test_modification): resolved - the fourth handler test is gone (lib count 206 -> 205) and no new unrecorded test path appears. Finding 2 (critical, the I-14 gate outside the write's lock): resolved at the lock-protocol level, not only in prose. Store::store_slack_submission (foundry-store/src/integrations/instance.rs:582) begins one transaction, calls lock_exclusive (:919, pg_advisory_xact_lock) first, reads CONNECTED_SLACK_WORKSPACES (:28) inside it, calls the caller's pure gate over that count and writes exactly one of the two plans in the same transaction; the handler's gate closure (handlers/instance.rs:1207) is SubmissionDoor::of over that count and holds no store call. A connection write takes the same advisory lock shared before its first row write (foundry-store/src/integrations/connections.rs:212 -> seal_fence_holds, instance.rs:936 pg_advisory_xact_lock_shared), so a workspace that finishes connecting is either committed before the count is read or waits behind the exclusive holder: the window the finding named is closed. Finding 4 (notice from the address): resolved - PageQuery, saved_notice and RawQuery are deleted, SavedNotice::answered (:422) inserts one wire name under the single session key 'integrations.slack_notice' and redirects to INSTANCE_PATH, show_instance reads it through taken_from (:432) which removes it as it reads, and no '?saved=' string remains anywhere under crates (grep). The session store is the shared PostgresStore (foundry-app/src/session.rs:73-77), so the notice reaches whichever replica answers her next read, as D16 now states. Finding 5 (false module doc): resolved - the paragraph now says the Slack doors answer a write with a redirect while Generate and Move answer in place, which matches answer(...) at :865. Finding 3 (stale L3): resolved by the design owner - architecture.md:1147 L3 now reads three closed facts and its table adds the no-app-in-effect case, matching SubmissionDoor::of (handlers/instance.rs:462-470), and F661 is bound in handoff.json to the S3 scenario 'Setting the same app up again finds Canzan Labs still connected' with a discriminating still_passes_if. Finding 6 (replica row stimulus): resolved - acceptance.md now reads 'two replicas, each of them holding the Slack app the instance admin entered, and she removes it', which is exactly the scenario's Given steps (feature:1023-1027). Finding 7 (stale S1 oracle approval): resolved - runs/review.oracle.S1-S3.json are re-approved at 371398e and committed at HEAD, so nwdes no longer refuses the close with OracleChanged.

Residuals examined and judged not defects, recorded so they are not mistaken for unexamined. (a) The gate's third fact, the app in effect, is still read from this replica's in-memory integrations snapshot (handlers/instance.rs:959, app_in_effect_of) rather than under the lock. That is the feature's declared convergence model - ADR-IIS-004's reload within 60 seconds, which the same snapshot already governs for the kept-secret rule - and the sealing box the two plans need comes from that same snapshot, so moving it under the lock would move sealing into the store against ADR-EIP-004. The narrow residual (a replica whose snapshot has not yet seen another replica's save, with a workspace connected through that save inside the same reload window) is inside the declared model, so no finding; it is named here as retained uncertainty rather than a clean claim. (b) Store::hold_pending_slack_app (foundry-store/src/integrations/instance.rs:563) now has no production caller: its only caller is crates/foundry-store/tests/iis_instance_store.rs:831, a recorded oracle locator that arranges a held app. Removing it would change immutable oracle bytes, so retaining it is correct and not dead-code clutter. (c) The one-shot notice is not consumed by show_slack_confirm's and show_slack_remove's fall-through to the instance page (:1007, :1082 answer(..., None, ...)), so a notice whose redirect was never followed can be read on a later visit to the instance page. That is ordinary flash semantics inside the admin's own session after her own real change, strictly narrower than the address-borne notice it replaced, and D16 states the one-shot contract; no finding. (d) D18's serialization claim rests on structural evidence - the lock protocol above and check-arch's seal-fence rule - not on a concurrency probe, because the recorded oracle is sequential; the declared verification commands are all GREEN, so this is not missing required evidence.

diagnostic: Accepted at 299f6e0. Every blocking finding of the rejected round is resolved in the corrected delta 730d6db..HEAD, and the resolutions are judged on the code and on this reviewer's own runs, not on the producer's report. The I-14 gate now decides inside the write's own transaction: Store::store_slack_submission takes pg_advisory_xact_lock exclusive first, reads the connected-workspace count there, calls the handler's pure SubmissionDoor gate over that count and commits exactly one of the two pre-sealed plans, while a connection write takes the same lock shared before its first row write - so the window that could switch an app under a connected workspace without I-14 is closed by the lock protocol, not by prose. The notice no longer comes from the address: PageQuery, saved_notice and RawQuery are gone, one wire name waits under a single key in the admin's own session in the shared Postgres session store and is removed as the page reads it, and no '?saved=' remains under crates. The unrecorded fourth handler test is deleted with no loss of coverage, and the false module paragraph is corrected. The design owner amended L3 to the three closed facts the gate actually decides over, added the no-app-in-effect case, bound F661 to the S3 scenario with a discriminating falsifier, recorded D16-D18, and corrected the replica-removal row's stimulus to its own Given steps; the S1-S3 oracle approvals are refreshed at 371398e, so the close is no longer refused. No oracle path changed in the delta - the feature file, the steps, the support and iis_instance_store.rs are byte-identical to 730d6db - and the only test-side edits are finding 1's own deletion and the required unreachable! stub rename in worker.rs, a behaviour-preserving migration to the new verb. All selected checks, every one executed by this reviewer on 299f6e0 in the shared local-dev VM, are GREEN: check-arch, foundry-app --lib 205/205, iis_instance_store 17/17, us-iis-05 29 scenarios / 364 steps, instance-integration-setup 105 scenarios / 1133 steps, and the two affected app integration targets iis_reload and iis_admin_cli_rotate 3/3. Oracle completeness against the original Request stands on unchanged oracle bytes, with both acceptance-record edits strengthening discrimination. Two non-blocking findings stay open for the acceptance designer - D16's negative half has no observing case, and L6/F203's version clause is witnessed by the handler read-table but not cited at the row - neither of which is a defect in the product or a gap against the Request; both are recorded with owner oracle and a remedy that needs no production change. Limits retained: Jev was unavailable (no TYPESAFE_API_KEY in this environment or a login shell, exit 3), so every owner and severity here is reviewer_reason; import metadata is absent, so exercised_changed_targets is unmeasured and coverage was judged by reading each stimulus and assertion; D18's serialization rests on the lock protocol and check-arch, not on a concurrency probe, because the recorded oracle is sequential; and the gate's app-in-effect fact is still read from the converging replica snapshot, which is inside the feature's declared 60-second reload model. No live oracle-owner session was discoverable from this role, so the two findings travel through the record (nwdes review findings --owner oracle) and this outcome to the root.
